chunks.arabic_text: صَالِحُ بْنُ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ قَيْسٍ بْنِ سَمْعَانَ بْنِ أَبِي ذَبِيحَةَ، مَوْلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ). رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ). غَالٍ، كَذَّابٌ، لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ.

translations.en: Sāliḥ b. ʿUqba b. Qays b. Samʿān b. Abī Dhabīḥa, client of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). He narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him). A ghālī, a liar, he is not turned to.

en.summary: Sāliḥ b. ʿUqba, a freed slave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his progeny), is recorded in al-Ghadāʾirī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* as a narrator of Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him). His classification as a *ghālī* (exaggerator) and *kadhdhāb* (liar) highlights the critical Shia methodology of distinguishing between mere narrators and those whose theological exaggerations or factual errors compromise the reliability of their reports for deriving religious law.
en.seo_question: Who is Sāliḥ b. ʿUqba and what is his status as a narrator in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.غَالٍ: One who exaggerates the virtues or status of the Imams, often beyond accepted limits
key_terms.لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ: Not turned to / not relied upon
